notes: Label granularity: 5-class attack-phase classification (Benign, Reconnaissance, Initial access, Lateral movement, Exfiltration); no binary benign/malicious experiment. Table IV (TM, STM, baselines) is the mean over the 5 validation folds of stratified CV on the 80% training split, not the held-out 20% test set. SMOTE is applied to the whole training split before the CV for the TM/STM only, so the TM/STM validation folds contain synthetic minority samples and are class-balanced, while the ML baselines (class weights, no SMOTE) are validated on imbalanced folds: Table IV TM vs baseline numbers are not on the same validation distribution, and TM CV scores may be optimistic. Tables V/VI do not state their split; Sec. IV says the 'test file' is loaded onto the Raspberry Pi. Host inference times (Table IV) are on an Apple M4 MacBook; Table VI on a Raspberry Pi 5. The text also mentions 'Keras framework built on TensorFlow 2.20.0' for all algorithms (Sec. VI-A); only TMU 0.6.5 is named as TM library (for the Pi). The STM clause scope is not determinable (no per-class figure for STM). Number of Boolean features is not given: 79 features x 40 bins would be 3160 but quantile KBinsDiscretizer may drop degenerate bins, so it is not recorded. Interpretability evidence also includes feature-level contribution scores (Fig. 6), i.e. feature_importance. NN baseline is printed with 'output layer=1 neurons' and softmax (Table III), presumably a typo.
